How it's treated: Order fulfilled (shipped), not voided, not a test. Month = order created date (UK time, +0100).
Tagged 'test' OR paid via 'Bogus Gateway (for testing)'. 7 Bogus-gateway orders carried no tag.
Paid but unfulfilled — left out until shipped (store policy). Export has no ship date, so shipped orders sit in their order month.
Prices include VAT at 20%; ex-VAT = amount / 1.20. Shopify's Taxes column = Total/6 on every order, confirming the rate.
Export 'Subtotal' is before discount (it equals the line items). Net goods = Subtotal − Discount Amount. Discounts allocated to products pro rata.
Kept out of revenue; shown separately (ex VAT, net of shipping refunds) because the accountant still needs it.
Amount refunded only (partial = partial). Assigned to the order's month. Applied to goods first; any excess over goods value treated as a shipping refund.
August refunds may still rise: late-August orders can still be refunded in September and would be counted back into August.
Marked 'refunded' but only GBP 30.00 of GBP 55.00 was refunded — counted as a GBP 30.00 refund.
Gift-card redemptions are counted as sales (as paid). No gift-card purchases appear in the export.
COGS / margin (no cost column), payment processor fees, payouts. Shopify Payments / PayPal settlements should be reconciled separately.
